info.bio:
El grupo fue fundado a finales de 1969 en Dublín (Irlanda), por el bajista y cantante Phil Lynott, el guitarrista Eric Bell, el organista Eric Wrixon y el baterista Brian Downey. Wrixon se fue en 1970, y cansados de las pocas posibilidades de éxito en Dublín, el grupo se fue a Londres en 1971.

Firmando un contrato con Decca Records, el primer éxito de Thin Lizzy llegó en 1973, con "Whiskey in the Jar", una versión de una tradicional canción irlandesa.

scenes.name: Jimi Hendrix
scenes.book: Heavy Metal: The Music and Its Culture
scenes.author: Deena Weinstein
scenes.desc: Intérprete de la tradición del blues eléctrico que ya había incorporado buena parte del estilo psicodélico, incluido su gusto por lo visual. Murió antes de que el heavy fuese un género definido, pero influyó enormemente en su música y su puesta en escena por su carisma y su talento, y porque encarnaba a la vez las dos tradiciones sobre las que se levanta el género. Con Cream introduce en el blues rock elementos del jazz, sobre todo los solos instrumentales extensos.

podcast.title: Chris Sangerides as Producer
podcast.body: Chris Sangerides, who produced The Tragically Hip's *Fully Completely*, was recognized for his previous work with Thin Lizzy, among other prominent heavy metal bands. "The producer was Chris Sangerides, a Greek Cypriot breads who was better known for working with Judas Priest and Black Sabbath and Ozzy and Thin Lizzy."

podcast.title: Early Influence of Traditional Irish Music
podcast.body: Formed in Dublin in 1970 as a rock band, Thin Lizzy incorporated traditional Irish music into their sound, especially evident in their first couple of records. "They were formed in 1970 as a rock band that drew on traditional Irish music for the first couple of records."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Impact on Irish Music Revival
podcast.body: Thin Lizzy, along with Horslips, faced considerable criticism from musical traditionalists in Ireland, yet they made significant contributions to a revival of interest in traditional Irish music. "Both Thin Lizzy and Horse-lips took a lot of abuse from the musical traditionalists of Ireland, but both contributed greatly to a revival of interest in traditional Irish music."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Influence on Metal and Rock
podcast.body: Thin Lizzy, through its member Phil Lynott, is referenced to underscore the "big debt" that metal in the 1980s owed to black artists, acknowledging their significant contributions to rock and its subgenres. "Phil Linatov, then Lizzie."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Chris Sangerides as Producer for Fully Completely
xref.body: Chris Sangerides, a Greek Cypriot, was chosen to produce *Fully Completely*. He was known for his work with heavy metal acts like Judas Priest, Black Sabbath, Ozzy, and Thin Lizzy, but The Tragically Hip were primarily drawn to the sound of records he produced for Concrete Blonde. The band felt disarmed by his lovely demeanor, and he showed his enthusiasm by traveling to Toronto to see them play at the Horseshoe Tavern before recording. Sangerides implemented a traditional 1970s recording technique, which was "completely alien" to the band's usual live-style approach, focusing on building tracks from the bass and drums upwards. "In my recollection, it was our idea to work with Chris, but in retrospect, I think Bruce Dickinson was very good at putting an idea out there and making you think that it was your own."

xref.title: Producer for The Tragically Hip's Fully Completely
xref.body: Chris Sangerides, a Greek Cypriot, produced The Tragically Hip's *Fully Completely*. He was known for working with heavy metal bands such as Judas Priest, Black Sabbath, Ozzy, and Thin Lizzy, but The Hip were specifically impressed by his work with Concrete Blonde. Sangerides was enthusiastic about producing *Fully Completely*, traveling to Toronto to see the band perform live before committing. He introduced a "traditional 1970s recording" approach, which was initially "completely alien" to The Hip, by stripping everything down and building tracks from the bass and drums up over three weeks, which resulted in a bigger, more isolated sound. "Chris really wanted to strip everything down in a way that I think is much more traditional 1970s recording, but for us it was completely alien."
